name: Uilenburger Synagoge
description: Built in 1766 for Amsterdam’s Ashkenazi Jewish community, the Uilenburgersjoel has a three-aisled synagogue hall above a lower room originally used for ritual slaughter. Its broad bell-shaped front gable faces a forecourt behind a street wall. The restored building now hosts Jewish cultural and social gatherings, concerts and other events.
